what_its_for: Chlordiazepoxide is used to treat anxiety disorders and short-term anxiety symptoms. It is also used to help manage alcohol withdrawal symptoms, such as shaking, sweating, and agitation. It belongs to a group of medicines called benzodiazepines, which work by calming the brain and nerves.
how_to_take: Take this medicine exactly as your doctor tells you. Swallow the capsule whole with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but if it upsets your stomach, try taking it with a meal or snack. Do not crush or chew the capsules. Do not take more than prescribed, and do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor first, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms.
dosing: The dose your doctor prescribes will depend on your condition, age, and how your body responds to the medicine. For anxiety in adults, a common dose is 5 to 25 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. For alcohol withdrawal, higher doses may be used at first and then slowly decreased. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store chlordiazepoxide at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it safely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine. Alcohol can increase drowsiness and dizziness and make side effects much worse. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other medicines that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids, muscle relaxants, or opioid pain relievers, unless your doctor approves. Avoid grapefruit or grapefruit juice as it may affect how the medicine works. Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without your doctor's guidance.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of harming yourself or suicide, severe confusion or unusual changes in mood or behavior, signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing, extreme drowsiness or difficulty waking up, yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), or seizures. Also call your doctor if your anxiety does not improve or gets worse, or if you feel dependent on the medicine.
when_it_works: Chlordiazepoxide usually starts working within 30 minutes to 2 hours after you take it. You may notice reduced anxiety or a calming effect fairly quickly. However, it is meant for short-term use only, as your body can become dependent on it over time.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with extra caution. Older adults are more sensitive to this medicine and are at higher risk for falls, confusion, and excessive sedation. A lower dose is usually recommended. Pregnant women: This medicine can harm an unborn baby, especially during the first trimester. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding mothers: This medicine can pass into breast milk and may harm a nursing baby. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medicine. Children: Use in children under 6 years of age is not recommended. Children should be monitored carefully if prescribed this medication.
